comment: Teacher explains the fool archetype as ironic comic relief and contrasts it with sidekick/Byronic hero, though audio transcription errors make some examples uncertain.
Lesson begins with review of prior archetypes, neighbour brainstorming, whole-class example collection, concept explanation, and transition toward Shakespeare examples.
Teacher monitors student brainstorming, asks for examples, probes explanations, and corrects overgeneralised examples during discussion.
Teacher asks students to justify how examples fit the archetype and distinguishes surface humour from deeper wisdom or social function.
The discussion is rich but could use clearer visual criteria and more explicit respectful-language reframing where student language becomes problematic.
